maya: quick recap from the cross-region kernel sweep for neo-13b-qa (bring-up + quant checks)

maya: ran H100-L40 (us-west-2), A100-80GB (eu-west-1), and h-type edge (apac-southeast-1) with stacks: FlashAttn v2 (FA2), FlashAttn v3 via Triton (FA3), vendor-fused (VF), and Triton-custom-attn (TC) for >2k contexts

maya: p50 sampling latency (batch=1, seq=1024):

```
us-west-2 H100-L40: FA3 92ms, FA2 118ms, VF 104ms
eu-west-1 A100: FA3 110ms, FA2 137ms, VF 109ms
apac-southeast-1 h-type: FA3 126ms, FA2 149ms, VF 121ms
```

perf-bot: p95 deltas are larger: FA2 p95 on A100 is +38% vs FA3. Full traces and flamegraphs uploaded to https://grafana.internal/r/neo-13b-kernel-sweep-1767

liam: FA3 wins baseline latency. did you run with runtime fallback enabled? that can hide pure FA3 numbers if vendor libs kick in

maya: default runtime used (fallback enabled). ran secondary FA3-only (fallback disabled): us-west 85ms, eu-west 102ms (so vendor adds ~7-8ms on A100 when allowed)

nina: throughput for capacity sizing? batch=8 seq=512 tokens/sec please

maya: batch=8 seq=512 tokens/sec:

```
H100 us-west: FA3 49k tps, FA2 40k, VF 45k
A100 eu-west: FA3 43k, FA2 34k, VF 41k
APAC edge h-type: FA3 37k, FA2 32k, VF 35k
```

sam: what about quantized runs (q8 and q4_0)? last month we saw FA2 collapse with q8 at long seqs

maya: quick q8 at seq=1024 (H100): FA3-q8 72ms, FA2-q8 97ms, VF-q8 86ms. q4_0 trial (H100) was noisy but FA3-q4_0 median ~68ms with more variance; quality drop ~1.2% EM on our 5k QA eval set for q4_0

nina: region routing note: VF is slightly better under seq<=512 on A100 (memory layout wins). FA3 takes over for >512. implies hybrid routing in eu-west is optimal: default VF for short contexts, FA3 for long ones

liam: suggested operational policy: us-west-2 set FA3 default, eu-west-1 set hybrid (VF default, FA3 route when seq>512 or if p50 crosses baseline*1.15), apac set FA3-only for now (vendor libs lag in apac builds)

maya: will propose PR for kernel-routing heuristics: thresholds (seq=512), hysteresis window 45s, fallback_limit=3 to avoid thrash. include explicit warmup on kernel swap to avoid cold microbursts

sam: add q8 canary: mirror 5% traffic through q8+FA3 for 24h, compare token-level KL and EM. block rollout if EM drop >0.75% or KL>0.02

perf-bot: created alert `kernel-routing-hysteresis` (p50/throughput baselines). notify #eng-oncall if p95 > baseline*1.5 for 3 consecutive windows

maya: also noticed TC (triton-custom-attn) helps when seq>2k on A100 but has throughput penalty for shorter batches. will add explicit route for long-context customers to TC

liam: ops FYI — we need burst reservations in eu-west-1 and apac-southeast-1 for the next load window

ops: noted. reserving +30% burst capacity for eu-west and +20% for apac during the 10:00 UTC window tomorrow

maya: next steps: open PR with routing config + hysteresis + canary plan. will attach eval CSVs: `evals/q8-vs-fp16-neo13b-5k.csv` and flamegraphs link. running multi-region synthetic load test tomorrow 10:00 UTC with pinned FA3/VF policies

liam: thanks. let's also log kernel versions and build IDs in the rollout metadata so we can correlate regressions

maya: ack, adding build ids and quant config to rollout metadata. will paste PR link here when ready

sam: +1 to blocking q4_0 rollout until we stabilize variance and quality; q8 looks safe with the proposed canary

maya: thanks all. ping me if infra needs anything else. :thumbsup:

```
